physics_goals.quote: The HOLMES experiment is aimed at directly measuring the electron neutrino mass using the EC decay of 163 Ho and an array of low temperature microcalorimeters.
physics_goals.value: Measure the electron neutrino mass calorimetrically from the electron-capture decay of 163Ho with an array of low-temperature microcalorimeters

summary.plain: An experiment in Italy that weighs the electron neutrino by watching holmium-163 atoms decay inside ultra-cold detectors. Its first result, from two months of data in 2025, limits the neutrino mass to 27 electron-volts at 90% credibility.
summary.technical: Calorimetric 163Ho electron-capture spectroscopy with ion-implanted TES microcalorimeters (6 eV FWHM, microwave-multiplexed readout) at a few tens of mK; ERC Advanced Grant 2014-2019 (INFN host); first result m_β < 27 eV/c² (90% credibility) from 7×10⁷ events.
